mazhabSelector.title: Choose your default madhab:
mazhabSelector.hint: A madhab is a school of Islamic law. Choose yours, and articles will show its opinions right away.
mazhabSelector.copyLink: Copy a link with this madhab
mazhabSelector.aboutIntro: A madhab is a school of Islamic law. The four Sunni schools agree on the foundations of the creed and differ on particular legal questions. The madhab you choose decides which opinion articles show by default.

descriptions.hanafi: Goes back to Abu Hanifa (699–767) of Kufa. The most widespread school: it is followed by Muslims in Turkey, Central Asia, the Volga region, the Caucasus, India and Pakistan. Known for its broad use of independent reasoning and analogy (qiyas).
descriptions.maliki: Goes back to Malik ibn Anas (711–795), the imam of Medina. It gives a special place to the practice of the people of Medina as a living continuation of the Sunnah. Widespread in North and West Africa.
descriptions.shafii: Founded by al-Shafi'i (767–820), the first to set out the principles of fiqh systematically. It keeps a strict order of sources: the Quran, the Sunnah, ijma, qiyas. Widespread in Egypt, East Africa, Southeast Asia, Dagestan and Chechnya.
descriptions.hanbali: Goes back to Ahmad ibn Hanbal (780–855). It relies most consistently on the Quran and the hadith and limits the role of independent reasoning. Widespread in the Arabian Peninsula.
